pr_title: kernel: add 'static' keyword to select routines (Auditable Branch)
pr_body:
Applies the 'static' keyword to the following inlined routines:
    z_priq_dumb_add()
    z_priq_mq_add()
    z_priq_mq_remove()
As those routines are only used in one place, they no longer have
externally visible declarations.

Signed-off-by: Peter Mitsis <peter.mitsis@intel.com>

Fixes #40438
pr_comments: @peter-mitsis  can we also submit this against the main branch please?

issue_context.title: Ill-formed sources due to external linkage inline functions calling static functions
issue_context.body:
In the Zephyr sources there are a few instances of static functions
used in inline functions with external linkage, which is ill-formed
for the C99 and later standards.  An example is static function
`sys_dlist_peek_head(sys_dlist_t*)`, which is used by
`void z_priq_dumb_add(sys_dlist_t *pq, struct k_thread *thread)`,
an always-inline function with external linkage.
To make the source well defined, the solution is to amend the definition
in kernel/sched.c from

ALWAYS_INLINE void `z_priq_dumb_add(sys_dlist_t *pq, struct k_thread *thread)`

to

static ALWAYS_INLINE void `z_priq_dumb_add(sys_dlist_t *pq, struct k_thread *thread)`

However, this would conflict with the (pointless?) declaration of the
function in `include/kernel/sched_priq.h`.  I think it is pointless because
`z_priq_dumb_add()` is only used in `kernel/sched.c`.  Thus a complete solution,
for this and a few other cases, would be to change the definitions
including the static storage class to the affected inline definitions
and remove the pointless declarations.

Please note that making the project well-formed as specified in the C
standards is a prerequisite for any form of MISRA compliance.
comments:
I did a search for ALWAYS_INLINE, and have found that in addition to z_priq_dumb_add() the following routines had declarations in sched_priq.h, but were only used in one file.
   - z_priq_mq_add()
   - z_priq_mq_remove()

As such, those two routines are also candidates for the same correction.

However, there is an additional routine about which I am not certain if it falls under the scope of this issue. The routine in question is z_unpend_thread_no_timeout(). This routine, defined in sched.c and using ALWAYS_INLINE, is declared in ksched.h but does not use ALWAYS_INLINE. (It's use is not confined to sched.c.) The question to which I am unsure of the answer is "Should the declaration for this routine also use ALWAYS_INLINE?".

Please advise.
Unless otherwise indicated, I'll leave z_unpned_thread_no_timeout() as is.
